reasoning:
CRM-88 is a web-only admin screen for managing ticket categories (add, rename, retire). The API endpoints are implemented in the parallel story CRM-87.

**Pattern Foundation**: `useTicketCategories.ts` reads categories; `SetUserPasswordPage.tsx` is the only existing admin-only screen and the template to follow. The new category screen mounts beside or as a sibling route.

**Auth & Authorization**: `useMe.ts` provides `isAdmin`, which is `undefined` until the session resolves—the screen must render neither controls nor "not available" text until it completes. `TicketQueuePage.test.tsx` and `SetUserPasswordPage.test.tsx` show how to test admin-only visibility.

**API Integration**: `client.ts` and `useRequest.ts` provide the HTTP layer and 4-state request hook for add/rename/retire mutations. `openapi.json`, `categories.test.js`, and `tickets.service.js` document the endpoints and server-side patterns.

**Forms & Error Handling**: `Field.tsx`, `Button.tsx`, `Input.tsx` build the form UI. No native HTML validators (API owns validation rules). `errors.ts` maps API responses to field-level error text (e.g., "name already taken" for duplicate rename).

**i18n (BR-6 requirement)**: `en.ts` and `ar.ts` hold all strings and must be edited in parallel in one commit; `parity.test.ts` enforces both languages have identical keys. `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` catches any JSX literals, including separators typed between tags.

**Routing & Navigation**: `routes.tsx` adds the new admin category route; `DeskShell.tsx` adds the nav entry. Hints emphasize the nav entry must be wired in with the screen, not added separately.

**Retire Confirmation UX**: Retiring is the one action that changes what other people see and cannot be undone from this screen, so it requires confirmation. Hints note no dialog primitive exists in `shared/ui/`, so this screen decides its confirmation approach (inline state, browser confirm, etc.) and documents the choice.

**Testing**: Use `stub-me.ts` to mock the `/me` endpoint. All API calls must use `useRequest` (already tested). Write tests for admin-only visibility, error cases, and the retire confirmation flow.

delta: # Story 88 — Admin scre

en to manage ticket categories (Story: CRM-88)

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-9-API (CRM-87)** merged: the API for adding, renaming and
retiring `ticket_categories` (`POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /api/v1/ticket-categories`) is live. The routes already exist at `api/src/

features/tickets/tickets.routes.js:54–66` behind `adminOnly` (mutations) and `requireStaff()` (list).
- **IDENTITY-2-API**

merged: `useMe()` returns `role` so `isAdmin` is meaningful.
- **CRM-50** merged: `web/src/pages/accounts/SetUserPasswordPage.tsx

` is the only precedent for an admin-only screen mounted on the shell — reuse its pattern for the isAdmin gate and shell nav entry.

## Story Goal

Give an admin a

single screen where they can:

1. See the current list of ticket categories.
2. Add a new category (name).
3. Rename an existing category.
4. Retire (soft-delete) a category,

after a confirmation this screen owns.

The list on the screen reflects each mutation without a full page reload. Non-admins land on a courteous refusal rather than seeing contro
ls the API will refuse (SC-2). Every string on the screen comes from `en.ts` and `ar.ts` (BR-6). No API change ships with this story — m

utations already audit (BR-2) and already soft-delete (BR-1) server-side.

**Not in scope:** any `api/` change (see TICKETS-9-API
/ CRM-87); reordering categories (they have no order); a shared dialog primitive in `shared/ui/` (this screen ow

ns its own confirmation).

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/accounts/SetUserPasswordPage.tsx` — the only precedent for a sh
ell-mounted admin-only screen. Read the whole file (short); copy the `useMe()`/`isAdmin` gate, the lo

ading placeholder while `isAdmin` is `undefined`, and the refusal branch when `isAdmin === false`.
2. `web/src/pages/accounts/SetUserPasswordPage.test.ts

x` — the test pattern (`renderWithProviders`, `signedIn: true`, admin vs non-admin, both languages). Match it for the new screen.
3. `web/src/pages/accoun
ts/useSetUserPassword.ts` — the tiny mutation hook shape (`useRequest`, POST to `/…`). Mirror this for `useAddCategory`, `

useRenameCategory`, `useRetireCategory`.
4. `web/src/shared/session/use-me.ts` (around lines 40–50) — read the `isAdmin` comment: it

is `undefined` until `/me` answers. Draw neither controls nor refusal in that state.
5. `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketCategories.ts` — the single existing reader of ticket categories (
used by `RaiseTicketPage.tsx:29` and `TicketQueuePage.tsx:286`). Extend or

re-export it so the admin screen has one authoritative reader; a second reader would be a second answer.
6. `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js` (lines 48–66) — conf
irm the URLs the client will hit: `POST /ticket-categories`, `PATCH /ticket-categories/:id`, `DELETE /ticket-categories/:id`, `GET /ticket-categories`. `request()` in `shared/api/client.

ts` already prefixes `/api/v1` (`shared/api/base-url.ts:3`).
7. `web/src/app/routes.tsx` (around lines 11 and 119) — read how `

SetUserPasswordPage` is imported and mounted. Add a sibling route for the new page.
8. `web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.tsx` (around line 91 — the `isAdmin === true` branch that

renders the "set password" admin link) — add a sibling nav link to the new screen next to it.
9. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — locate the exist
ing `accounts` (or nearest admin) sub-object and mirror the shape. Both files are one-level-deep nested objects with

camelCase leaves.
10. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` and `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — the two tests that fail if BR-6 is bro

ken. Do not disable them; add keys in both language files in the same edit.
11. `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` — the four-state contract (`idle |

loading | success | error`); errors carry `fields`. Reuse verbatim.
12. `web/src/pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` — the reference for wrapping an

interpolated value with U+2068 … U+2069 when a category name appears inside a translated sentence (retire confirmation, duplicate-name error).
13. `web/src/testing/render.tsx` and `web
/src/testing/stub-me.ts` — the shell requires `/me` to be stubbed. Every test in this story that ren

ders under providers must stub it (as admin, as non-admin, and as loading).
14. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — read
the L-30 (fresh `Response` per fetch call), L-51 (bidi isolate around interpolated values) and L-55

(never a native validator) entries; the tests below enforce them.

Grep hints (cheap):

- `grep -n "is

Admin" web/src` — see every use site.
- `grep -n "useTicketCategories" web/src` — see who reads categories today.
- `grep -n "

ticket-categories" api/src` — confirm the URL shape.

## Product rules (from story)

- **BR-1 (soft delete):** en
forced by `DELETE /ticket-categories/:id` — the client sends the delete; the API sets `deleted_at`. The client does not attempt a

hard delete and does not surface a "restore" button.
- **BR-2 (audit):** enforced by the API. The client does not compute or send before/after — the server

does.
- **BR-6 (resource files):** every visible string in this screen lives in `en.ts` and `ar.ts`; `parity.test.

ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` prove it.
- **SC-2 (courtesy, not enforcement):** the non-admin branch reads as an explanation,

not a lock. Enforcement stays on the server.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Extend the categories reader (single source)

**

File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketCategories.ts`

- Keep the current default export/behaviour used by `RaiseTicketPage` and `TicketQueuePage` unchanged.
- Add a
`refetch()` (or return a `reload` function from the underlying `useRequest`) so the admin screen can re-read

the list after each mutation without a full page reload. Do **not** duplicate the reader in a new file — a second reader would be a second answer to "what are the categories".
- Types: expose `{
id: string; name: string }[]` for active categories (the API `GET /ticket-categories` already filters `deleted_at IS NULL` — do not filter again

on the client).

### 2 — Three mutation hooks

**Create files** under `web/src/pages/tickets/`:

- `useAddCategory.ts` — `POST /ticket-categories`, body `{ name }`.

- `useRenameCategory.ts` — `PATCH /ticket-categories/:id`, body `{ name }`.
- `useRetireCategory.ts` — `DELETE /ticket-categories/:id`.

Each hook:

- Wraps `useRequ

est` (the four-state hook: `idle | loading | success | error`; error carries `fields`).
- Calls `request()` from `shared/api/client.ts` — do **not** prefix `/api/v1` (already prefixed).
- Retur

ns `{ state, run, reset }`. No second request shape.

### 3 — The screen

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/Manage

CategoriesPage.tsx`

Behaviour:

1. `const { isAdmin } = useMe();`
   - `undefined` → render

the shell-consistent skeleton (`shared/ui/Skeleton`) — no controls, no refusal.
   - `false` → render the refusal `
<EmptyState />` (a courteous sentence from `t.categories.notAdmin`), matching `SetUserPassword

Page.tsx:30`.
   - `true` → render the manager.
2. Manager layout (use `shared/ui/Stack`, `Card`, `Heading`, `Text

`, `Field`, `Input`, `Button`):
   - Heading + short description.
   - **Add** form: single `Field` with `Input` (no `required`, no `pattern`, no native validator — L-55

(read-only).
     - "Rename" affordance → toggles the row into an inline `Input` + Save/Cancel. Save

calls `useRenameCategory`, then `refetch()`.
     - "Retire" button → opens **this screen's own** confirmation panel (see §

4).
3. Error surfacing:
   - Field errors from `error.fields.name` render under the `Input`.
   - Duplicate-name error (the shared code from the API's category
rule set): map to `t.categories.errors.nameTaken` — do **not** fall back to `t.errors[code]` blindly (the shared sentence is gener
ic; the taken-name sentence belongs to this screen because two other screens have already needed their own sentence for a shared code).

- Any other error uses `t.errors[code]` as a default.
4. Interpolation: when the API returns the offending value or the confirmation quotes a category name, w

rap the value with U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51 — see `pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts`).

### 4 — Retire confirmation

- No d

ialog primitive lives in `shared/ui/` today; do **not** invent one.
- Implement as an inline confirmation panel that replaces the row's action buttons:
`t.categories.retire.confirm` (a sentence quoting the name via the bidi isolate) plus a destructive **Confirm** and a
**Cancel** button. Document the choice in a comment at the top of `ManageCategoriesPage.tsx`: "no shared dialog primitive; inline conf

irmation keeps focus and screen-reader flow inside the row; a modal would need a shared component this codebase does not have."
- Only "

Retire" asks first. "Add" and "Rename" apply on submit.

### 5 — Route and nav entry

**File

:** `web/src/app/routes.tsx`

- Import `ManageCategoriesPage` next to `SetUserPasswordPage` (near line 11).
- Add a sibling route (e.g. path `/admin/ticket-categories
`) modelled on the `SetUserPasswordPage` mounting around line 119. Wrap in `<RequireAuth>` the same way that route

is wrapped.

**File:** `web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.tsx`

- In the `isAdmin === true` branch (around line 91, next to the "Set password" link), add

a nav link to the new route. Label from `t.shell.nav.manageCategories`.
- **Do not** add the link outside that branch —

a route only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist, and drawing it for non-admins would violate SC-2.

### 6 — i18n keys (both files, same

edit)

**Files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

Add a `categories` sub-object (one level deep, camelCase lea

ves). Suggested keys:

- `title`, `description`
- `addLabel`, `addPlaceholder`, `addSubmit`, `addSuccess`
- `renameLabel`, `renameSubmit`, `renameCancel`, `renameS

uccess`
- `retireAction`, `retire.confirm` (sentence containing the name), `retire.confirmSubmit`, `retire.cancel`, `retire.success`
- `empty` (no

categories yet)
- `notAdmin` (courtesy sentence for non-admins)
- `errors.nameTaken` (this screen's own sentence for the duplicate-name code)

Add a matching `shell.nav.

manageCategories` label.

Both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` must gain the same keys in the same commit or `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` fails.

## Backend Tasks

**
No backend changes required.** The routes at `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js:54–66` are the contract; audit (BR-2) and soft delete (BR-1) live
on the server. If the API is missing a duplicate-name error code or the `GET` list shape does not match, that is a TICKETS-9-API (CRM-87

forced in `ManageCategoriesPage.tsx` (mirrors `SetUserPasswordPage.tsx:30`).
- **Empty list:** render `t.categories.empty` inside an `E

mptyState`; the add form is still available.
- **Duplicate name on Add / Rename:** the API returns a validation error with a `fields.name` entry and a shared code. Render `

t.categories.errors.nameTaken` and mark the field.
- **Concurrent rename (someone else renamed the same category between our GET and PATCH):** the server answers with a not

-found or conflict; surface `t.errors[code]` and `refetch()`.
- **Retire race (already retired):** the DELETE returns 404 or

409; surface the code, `refetch()`, drop the row.
- **Network failure:** `useRequest` → `error` state; keep the row in view; show `

t.errors.network` (the existing key).
- **Non-admin who guessed the URL:** the screen shows `notAdmin` (courtesy) — enforc

ement stays on the API's `adminOnly` guard (`tickets.routes.js:54–62`).
- **RTL rendering of a Latin category name inside an Arabic sentence:** wrap the inter

polated value in U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51).
- **Unicode / whitespace names:** do not trim client-side beyond remov
ing leading/trailing whitespace before send; do not enforce a length or character class on the client — that is the API's rule (

L-55).
- **A fetch stub in a test returning the same `Response` twice:** guaranteed break. Build a fresh `Response` per call (L-30).

## Test Plan

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/ManageCategoriesPage.test.tsx` (new) — Vitest + Testing Library, using `renderWithProviders` and `stubMe` from

`web/src/testing/`.

1. **Renders a skeleton while `/me` is pending** (isAdmin `undefined`): neither the add form nor the refusal is in

the DOM.
2. **Non-admin sees the refusal**, in both `en` and `ar`; no add/rename/retire controls exist.
3. **Adm

in sees the list** — stub `GET /ticket-categories` with two categories; both names render.
4. **Add** — f
ill and submit; assert POST body `{ name }`; new list `refetch`ed

; success sentence shown; field cleared.
5. **Duplicate-name error on Add** — API returns validation error with `fields.name`; assert `t.categories.errors.nameTaken` renders (not the shared `

t.errors[…]`); field is marked.
6. **Rename** — click Rename on row, edit, save; assert PATCH URL and body; new name in list.
7. **Retire
asks first** — click Retire; the inline confirmation appears with the name wrapped in U+2068/U+2069; Cancel leaves the list unchanged; Confirm calls DELETE and

removes the row.
8. **No native validator** — the `Input` has neither `required` nor `pattern` nor `type="email"` (guard against L-55; asserted via D

OM attribute checks).
9. **Fresh `Response` per fetch call** in every stub (L-30) — mirror the pattern in `S

etUserPasswordPage.test.tsx`.

**Existing tests that should be re-run and must still pass:**

- `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` — proves every

new key exists in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.
- `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — proves no literal string leaked into JSX (including separators between t

ags).
- `web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.test.tsx` — the new admin nav link must not break existing shell assertions; add a case

that admin sees it and non-admin does not.
- `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` — add a case that `/admin/ticket-

categories` mounts the page for an admin and refuses for a non-admin.
- `web/src/pages/tickets/RaiseTicketPage.test.tsx` and `TicketQueuePage.test.tsx`

— must still pass after `useTicketCategories` gains a `refetch` return (backward compatible shape).

## Migration / Rollback

Not applicable — no schema change
and no persistent client state. Rollback is a code revert; the API routes remain live for other cl

ients.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — all suites green (including the new file,

parity, no-hardcoded-strings, routing, and shell tests).
2. **Frontend typechecks + builds:** `cd web && npm run build` — this runs `tsc -b

&& vite build`; `npm test` alone does **not** typecheck.
3. **Backend regression:** `cd api && npm test` — no backend files touched; confirm nothing broke

by import graph.
4. **No AI attribution:** `git diff --staged | grep -iE "co-?authored-by:
.*(claude|gpt|copilot|anthropic|openai|ai[- ]assist)"` returns nothing; `grep -R
niE "generated by (an )?ai|written by (an )?ai|co-?authored-by:.*(claude|copilot|

gpt)" web/src api/src docs` returns nothing new.
5. **Manual smoke:** `cd web && npm run dev`, sign in as an admin from the seed,
navigate via the new shell link, add / rename / retire a category, refresh — persisted state matches. Sign in as staff (

non-admin), visit the URL directly, confirm the refusal renders.
6. **RTL smoke:** switch language to Arabic in the shell; retire a category with a Latin

name — the name renders as one bidi unit inside the Arabic sentence (U+2068/U+2069 in place).

## Done Criteria

- [ ]

`ManageCategoriesPage.tsx` exists under `web/src/pages/tickets/` and is mounted from `routes.tsx` at an admin-only path.
- [ ] Admin nav link added in `D

eskShell.tsx` inside the `isAdmin === true` branch, and only there.
- [ ] Add, rename, and retire mutations use dedicated `useRequest`-based hooks

; each round-trips to the existing API routes at `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js:54–62`.
- [ ] List

refreshes after every mutation without a full page reload (single reader: `useTicketCategories`).
- [ ] Retire asks first via an inline confirmation this screen owns; the

confirmation quotes the name inside U+2068 … U+2069.
- [ ] Non-admin sees a courtesy refusal (SC-2); `isAdmin === undefined` renders only a skeleton.

- [ ] All new strings live in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`; `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` pass.
- [ ] No native validator attributes (`required`, `

pattern`, `type="email"`, `min`, `max`) on the form (L-55).
- [ ] `cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both green; `cd api && npm test` still green.
- [ ] No AI-attribution str

ings in commits or diffs.
